newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chrysler says Feb U.S. sales look stagnant.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler says Feb U.S. sales look stagnant.

text.p: Chrysler Corp vice chairman Robert Lutz said on Monday he believed the U.S. car market in February was stagnant and that a difficult time in March could prompt carmakers to revise downward their sales forecasts.

"With February complete, the U.S. market looks fairly stagnant and a lot of European markets are sliding backwards," Lutz told Reuters in an interview after a speech to the American International Club of Geneva.

"After the first two months (of the year), I would have to say that all bets are off because the markets around the world do not look that robust," said Lutz, who was in Switzerland for the Geneva car show.
Chrysler is scheduled to report car sales for February later on Monday. The carmaker in January reported a sales gain of two percent to 168,157 passenger vehicles and light trucks.
Lutz said Chrysler "might see fit to modify" its forecasts for 1997 if sales in March are weak.

Chrylser does not make public its internal sales forecasts but Chrysler chief executive Robert Eaton said in January that the carmaker should exceed the record 1996 worldwide sales of 2.97 million vehicles.
"It is not a bad market," Lutz said of current industry conditions. "It has just deflated a bit from a great market."
